Chapter 3   第三章
Multiple Coordinate Spaces
多重坐标空间
The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places;
我所定的地界，处处美好；
surely I have a delightful inheritance.
我的确拥有令人愉快的遗产。
— Psalm 16:6 (New International Version)
— 诗篇 16:6（新国际版）

Chapter 1 discussed how we can establish a coordinate space anywhere we want simply by picking a point to be the origin and deciding how we want the axes to be oriented. We usually don't make these decisions arbitrarily; we form coordinate spaces for specific reasons (one might say “different spaces for different cases”). This chapter gives some examples of common coordinate spaces that are used for graphics and games. We will then discuss how coordinate spaces are nested within other coordinate spaces.
第一章讨论了如何通过简单地选择一个点作为原点并决定坐标轴的方向，在任何我们想要的地方建立一个坐标空间。我们通常不会随意做出这些决定；我们会出于特定的原因构建坐标空间（有人可能会说“不同的情况需要不同的坐标空间”）。本章给出了一些用于图形和游戏的常见坐标空间的示例。然后，我们将讨论坐标空间如何嵌套在其他坐标空间中。

This chapter introduces the idea of multiple coordinate systems. It is divided into five main sections.
本章介绍多重坐标系的概念。本章主要分为五个部分。

  • Section 3.1 justifies the need for multiple coordinate systems.
    第 3.1 节证明了多个坐标系的必要性。
  • Section 3.2 introduces some common coordinate systems. The main concepts introduced are
    3.2 节介绍了一些常见的坐标系。主要介绍的概念有
    • world space   世界空间
    • object space   物体空间
    • camera space   相机空间
    • upright space   直立空间
  • Section 3.3 describes coordinate-space transformations.
    第 3.3 节描述坐标空间变换。
    • Section 3.3.1 exposes a duality between two ways of thinking about coordinate-space transformations.
      第 3.3.1 节揭示了坐标空间变换的两种思维方式的二元性。
    • Section 3.3.2 describes how to specify one coordinate system in terms of another.
      第 3.3.2 节描述了如何根据一个坐标系来指定另一个坐标系。
    • Section 3.3.3 discusses the very important concept of basis vectors.
      第 3.3.3 节讨论了基向量这个非常重要的概念。
  • Section 3.4 discusses nested coordinate spaces, commonly used for animating hierarchically segmented objects in 3D space.
    第 3.4 节讨论嵌套坐标空间，通常用于在 3D 空间中为分层分割的对象制作动画。
  • Section 3.5 is a political campaign for more human readable code.
    第 3.5 节是一场争取更加人性化可读的代码的政治运动。

3.1Why Bother with Multiple Coordinate Spaces?
3.1 为什么要使用多个坐标空间？

Why do we need more than one coordinate space? After all, any one 3D coordinate system extends infinitely and thus contains all points in space. So we could just pick a coordinate space, declare it to be the “world” coordinate space, and all points could be located using this coordinate space. Wouldn't that be easier? In practice, the answer to this is “no.” Most people find it more convenient to use different coordinate spaces in different situations.
为什么我们需要多个坐标空间？毕竟，任何一个三维坐标系都是无限延伸的，因此包含了空间中的所有点。所以我们可以直接选择一个坐标空间，将其声明为“世界”坐标空间，然后所有点都可以在这个坐标空间中定位。这样不是更简单吗？实际上，答案是“不”。大多数人认为在不同情况下使用不同的坐标空间更方便。

The reason multiple coordinate spaces are used is that certain pieces of information are known only in the context of a particular reference frame. It might be true that theoretically all points could be expressed using a single “world” coordinate system. However, for a certain point a , we may not know the coordinates of a in the “world” coordinate system. But we may be able to express a relative to some other coordinate system.
使用多个坐标空间的原因是，某些信息仅在特定参考系的上下文中才为人所知。理论上，所有点都可以用一个“世界”坐标系来表示，这或许没错。然而，对于某个点 a ，我们可能不知道 a 在“世界”坐标系中的坐标。但我们或许能够相对于其他坐标系来表示 a 。

For example, the residents of Cartesia (see Section 1.2.1) use a map of their city with the origin centered quite sensibly at the center of town and the axes directed along the cardinal points of the compass. The residents of Dyslexia use a map of their city with the coordinates centered at an arbitrary point and the axes running in some arbitrary directions that probably seemed a good idea at the time. The citizens of both cities are quite happy with their respective maps, but the State Transportation Engineer assigned the task of running up a budget for the first highway between Cartesia and Dyslexia needs a map showing the details of both cities, which therefore introduces a third coordinate system that is superior to him, though not necessarily to anybody else. Each major point on both maps needs to be converted from the local coordinates of the respective city to the new coordinate system to make the new map.
例如，笛卡尔城 (参见 1.2.1 节) 的居民使用的城市地图，其原点合理地位于城镇中心，坐标轴沿着罗盘的基本点。迪斯莱西亚城的居民使用的城市地图，其坐标以任意点为中心，坐标轴指向任意方向，这在当时看来可能是个好主意。这两个城市的居民都对各自的地图很满意，但是负责为笛卡尔城和迪斯莱西亚城之间的第一条高速公路编制预算的州交通工程师需要一张显示两个城市细节的地图，因此引入了第三个坐标系，这个坐标系比他更优越，但不一定比任何人都优越。两张地图上的每个主要点都需要从各自城市的当地坐标转换为新的坐标系，以制作新地图。

The concept of multiple coordinate systems has historical precedent. While Aristotle (384–322 BCE), in his books On the Heavens and Physics, proposed a geocentric universe with Earth at the origin, Aristarchus (ca. 310–230 BCE) proposed a heliocentric universe with the sun at the origin. So we can see that more than two millennia ago the choice of coordinate system was already a hot topic for discussion. The issue wasn't settled for another couple of millennia until Nicolaus Copernicus (1473–1543) observed in his book De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium (On the Revolutions of the Celestial Orbs) that the orbits of the planets can be explained more simply in a heliocentric universe without all the mucking about with wheels within wheels in a geocentric universe.
多重坐标系的概念由来已久。亚里士多德（公元前 384-322 年）在其著作《天体论》和《物理学》中提出了以地球为原点的地心说宇宙观，而阿里斯塔克斯（约公元前 310-230 年）则提出了以太阳为原点的日心说宇宙观。由此可见，两千多年前，坐标系的选择就已成为一个热门话题。这个问题又持续了几千年，直到尼古拉·哥白尼（1473-1543 年）在其著作《天体运行论》中指出，行星的轨道可以用日心说宇宙观更简单地解释，而不必像地心说宇宙观那样费力地推导。

In Sand-Reckoner, Archimedes (d. 212 BCE), perhaps motivated by some of the concepts introduced in Section 1.1, developed a notation for writing down very large numbers—numbers much larger than anybody had ever counted at that time. Instead of choosing to count dead sheep, as in Section 1.1, he chose to count the number of grains of sand it would take to fill the universe. (He estimated that it would take 8×10 63 grains of sand, but he did not, however, address the question of where he would get the sand.) In order to make the numbers larger, he chose not the geocentric universe generally accepted at the time, but Aristarchus' revolutionary new heliocentric universe. In a heliocentric universe, Earth orbits the sun, in which case the fact that the stars show no parallax means that they must be much farther away than Aristotle could ever have imagined. To make his life more difficult, Archimedes deliberately chose the coordinate system that would produce larger numbers. We will use the direct opposite of his approach. In creating our virtual universe inside the computer we will choose coordinate systems that make our lives easier, notharder.
在《沙算术》一书中，阿基米德（卒于公元前 212 年）或许是受到 1.1 节中引入的一些概念的启发，发明了一种用于记录非常大的数字的符号——这些数字远超当时任何人所能计算的数字。他没有像 1.1 节中那样选择数死羊，而是选择数填满宇宙所需的沙粒数量。（他估计需要 8×10 63 粒沙粒，但他并没有回答这些沙粒从何而来的问题。）为了使数字更大，他选择的不是当时普遍接受的地心说宇宙观，而是阿里斯塔克斯革命性的新日心说宇宙观。在日心说宇宙观中，地球绕太阳运行，在这种情况下，恒星没有视差，这意味着它们与地球的距离一定比亚里士多德所能想象的要远得多。为了让计算更加复杂，阿基米德特意选择了能够产生更大数字的坐标系。我们将使用与他的方法完全相反的方法。在计算机内部创建虚拟世界时，我们将选择使我们的生活更轻松而不是更困难的坐标系。

In today's enlightened times, we are accustomed to hearing in the media about cultural relativism, which promotes the idea that it is incorrect to consider one culture or belief system or national agenda to be superior to another. It's not too great a leap of the imagination to extend this to what we might call “transformational relativism”—the contention that no place or orientation or coordinate system can be considered superior to others. In a certain sense that's true, but to paraphrase George Orwell in Animal Farm: “All coordinate systems are considered equal, but some are more equal than others.” Now let's look at some examples of common coordinate systems that you will meet in 3D graphics.
在当今这个启蒙时代，我们习惯于在媒体上听到关于文化相对主义的报道，这种观点宣扬一种文化、信仰体系或国家议程优于其他文化、信仰体系或国家议程是错误的。将其延伸到我们所谓的“转型相对主义”并非难事，它认为没有任何地点、方向或坐标系可以被认为优于其他。从某种意义上说，这的确没错，但套用乔治·奥威尔在《动物庄园》中的话来说：“所有坐标系都被认为是平等的，但有些坐标系比其他坐标系更平等。”现在，让我们看一些在 3D 图形中常见的坐标系示例。

3.2Some Useful Coordinate Spaces
3.2 一些有用的坐标空间

Different coordinate spaces are needed because some information is meaningful or available only in a particular context. In this section, we give some examples of common coordinate spaces.
由于某些信息仅在特定上下文中才有意义或可用，因此需要不同的坐标空间。在本节中，我们给出一些常见坐标空间的示例。

3.2.1World Space  3.2.1 世界空间

The authors wrote this book in 2011 from Chicago, Illinois, and Denton, Texas. More precisely, their locations were as shown in Table 3.1.
本书作者于 2011 年在美国伊利诺伊州芝加哥和德克萨斯州登顿撰写。更准确地说，他们的具体位置如表 3.1 所示。

Author  作者 City  城市 Latitude  纬度 Longitude  经度
Fletcher  弗莱彻 Chicago  芝加哥 41°57' North  北 87°39' West  西方
Ian  伊恩 Denton  丹顿 33°11' North  北 97° West  西方
Table 3.1  表 3.1Locations of authors, including a random offset introduced to protect us from our many obsessive stalker fans.
作者的位置，包括引入的随机偏移量，以保护我们免受众多痴迷的跟踪狂粉丝的侵害。

These latitude and longitude values express our “absolute” position in the world. You don't need to know where Denton, Chicago, Texas, Illinois, or even the United States is to use this information because the position is absolute. The origin, or (0,0) point, in the world was decided for historical reasons to be located on the equator at the same longitude as the Royal Observatory in the town of Greenwich, England.
这些经纬度值表达了我们在世界上的“绝对”位置。您无需知道丹顿、芝加哥、德克萨斯州、伊利诺伊州，甚至美国的具体位置，即可使用此信息，因为该位置是绝对的。由于历史原因，世界上的原点（或 (0,0) 点）被确定为赤道上与英国格林威治皇家天文台相同的经度。

(The astute reader will note that these coordinates are not Cartesian coordinates, but rather they are spherical coordinates—see Section 7.3.2. That is not significant for this discussion. We live in a flat 2D world wrapped around a sphere, a concept that supposedly eluded most people until Christopher Columbus verified it experimentally.)
（敏锐的读者会注意到，这些坐标不是笛卡尔坐标，而是球面坐标——参见第 7.3.2 节。这对于本次讨论并不重要。我们生活在一个被球体包裹的平坦二维世界中，据说这个概念在克里斯托弗·哥伦布通过实验证实之前一直不为大多数人所理解。）

The world coordinate system is a special coordinate system that establishes the “global” reference frame for all other coordinate systems to be specified. In other words, we can express the position of other coordinate spaces in terms of the world coordinate space, but we cannot express the world coordinate space in terms of any larger, outer coordinatespace.
世界坐标系是一个特殊的坐标系，它为所有其他待定义的坐标系建立了“全局”参考框架。换句话说，我们可以用世界坐标空间来表示其他坐标空间的位置，但不能用任何更大的外部坐标空间来表示世界坐标空间。

In a nontechnical sense, the world coordinate system establishes the “biggest” coordinate system that we care about, which in most cases is not actually the entire world. For example, if we wanted to render a view of Cartesia, then for all practical purposes Cartesia would be “the world,” since we wouldn't care where Cartesia is located (or even if it exists at all). To find the optimal way to pack automobile parts into a box, we might write a physics simulation that “jiggles” a box full of parts around until they settle. In this case we confine our “world” to the inside of a box. So in different situations the world coordinate space will define a different “world.”
从非技术角度来看，世界坐标系建立了我们关心的“最大”坐标系，在大多数情况下，这实际上并非整个世界。例如，如果我们想要渲染笛卡尔的视图，那么实际上笛卡尔就是“世界”，因为我们并不关心笛卡尔位于何处（甚至不在乎它是否存在）。为了找到将汽车零件装入盒子的最佳方法，我们可能会编写一个物理模拟程序，让装满零件的盒子“摇晃”起来，直到它们稳定下来。在这种情况下，我们将“世界”限制在盒子内部。因此，在不同情况下，世界坐标空间将定义不同的“世界”。

We've said that world coordinate space is used to describe absolute positions. We hope you pricked up your ears when you heard this, and you knew we weren't being entirely truthful. We already discussed in Section 2.4.1 that there's really no such thing as “absolute position.” In this book, we use the term “absolute” to mean “absolute with respect to the largest coordinate space we care about.” In other words, “absolute” to us actually means “expressed in the world coordinate space.”
我们说过，世界坐标空间用于描述绝对位置。希望您听到这句话时能竖起耳朵，并知道我们并非完全诚实。我们已经在 2.4.1 节讨论过，实际上并不存在“绝对位置”。在本书中，我们使用“绝对”一词来表示“相对于我们关心的最大坐标空间的绝对位置”。换句话说，对我们来说，“绝对”实际上意味着“在世界坐标空间中表达”。

The world coordinate space is also known as the global or universal coordinate space.
世界坐标空间也称为全局或通用坐标空间。

3.2.2Object Space  3.2.2 对象空间

Object space is the coordinate space associated with a particular object. Every object has its own independent object space. When an object moves or changes orientation, the object coordinate space associated with that object is carried along with it, so it moves or changes orientation too. For example, we all carry our own personal coordinate system around with us. If we were to ask you to “take one step forward,” we are giving you an instruction in your object space. (Please forgive us for referring to you as an object—you know what we mean.) We have no idea which way you will move in absolute terms. Some of you will move north, some south, and those wearing magnet boots on the side of a building might move upward! Concepts such as “forward,” “back,” “left,” and “right” are meaningful in object coordinate space. When someone gives you driving directions, sometimes you will be told to “turn left” and other times you will be told to “go east.” “Turn left” is a concept that is expressed in object space, and “go east” is expressed in world space.
对象空间是与特定对象关联的坐标空间。每个对象都有自己独立的对象空间。当对象移动或改变方向时，与该对象关联的对象坐标空间也会随之移动或改变方向。例如，我们每个人都随身携带着自己的坐标系。如果我们要求你“向前迈一步”，我们实际上是在向你的对象空间发出指令。（请原谅我们将你称为一个对象——你明白我们的意思。）我们无法确切地知道你会朝哪个方向移动。有些人会向北移动，有些人会向南移动，而那些穿着磁力靴站在建筑物侧面的人可能会向上移动！诸如“前进”、“后退”、“左转”和“右转”之类的概念在对象坐标空间中是有意义的。当有人给你指路时，有时你会被告知“左转”，有时你会被告知“向东走”。“左转”是在对象空间中表达的概念，而“向东走”是在世界空间中表达的概念。

Locations as well as directions can be specified in object space. For example, if I asked you where the muffler on your car was, you wouldn't tell me “Cambridge,1 MA,” even if you were Tom or Ray Magliozzi and your car was actually in Cambridge. In this case, an answer expressed with a global perspective like this is totally useless;2 I want you to express the location of your muffler in the object space of your car.
位置和方向都可以在对象空间中指定。例如，如果我问你汽车的消声器在哪里，你不会告诉我“马萨诸塞州剑桥市”，即使你是汤姆或雷·马格里奥齐，而且你的车实际上在剑桥。在这种情况下，像这样用全局视角表达的答案完全没用；我希望你表达消声器在你汽车的对象空间中的位置。

In the context of graphics, object space is also known as model space, since the coordinates for the vertices of a model are expressed in model space. Object space is also known as body space, especially in physics contexts. It's also common to use a phrase like “with respect to the body axes,” which means the same thing as “expressed using body space coordinates.”
在图形学中，对象空间也称为模型空间，因为模型顶点的坐标是在模型空间中表示的。对象空间也称为体空间，尤其是在物理领域。“相对于体轴”这样的表述也很常见，其含义与“用体空间坐标表示”相同。

3.2.3Camera Space  3.2.3 相机空间

One especially important example of an object space is camera space, which is the object space associated with the viewpoint used for rendering. In camera space, the camera is at the origin, with +x pointing to the right, +z pointing forward (into the screen, the direction the camera is facing), and +y pointing “up.” (Not “up” with respect to the world, “up” with respect to the top of the camera.) Figure 3.1 shows a diagram of camera space.
对象空间的一个特别重要的例子是相机空间，它是与用于渲染的视点相关联的对象空间。在相机空间中，相机位于原点， +x 指向右侧， +z 指向前方（朝向屏幕，即相机朝向的方向）， +y 指向“上方”。（不是相对于世界坐标的“上方”，而是相对于相机顶部的“上方”。）图 3.1 展示了相机空间的示意图。

Figure 3.1  图 3.1Camera space using left-handed conventions
使用左手约定的相机空间

These are the traditional left-handed conventions; others are common. In particular, the OpenGL tradition is right-handed, with −z pointing into the screen and +z coming out of the screen towards the viewer.
这些是传统的左手惯用手法；其他的也很常见。特别是，OpenGL 的传统是右手惯用手法，其中 −z 指向屏幕内部，而 +z 指向屏幕外部，朝向观看者。

Note carefully the differences between camera space, which is a 3D space, and screen space, which is a 2D space. The mapping of camera-space coordinates to screen-space coordinates involves an operation known as projection. We'll discuss camera space in more detail, and this conversion process in particular, when we talk about coordinate spaces used in rendering in Section 10.3.
仔细注意相机空间（三维空间）和屏幕空间（二维空间）之间的区别。相机空间坐标到屏幕空间坐标的映射涉及一个称为投影的操作。我们将在 10.3 节讨论渲染中使用的坐标空间时更详细地讨论相机空间，特别是这个转换过程。

3.2.4Upright Space  3.2.4 直立空间

Sometimes the right terminology is the key to unlocking a better understanding of a subject. Don Knuth coined the phrase “name and conquer” to refer to the common and important practice in mathematics and computer science of giving a name to a concept that is used frequently. The goal is to avoid repeating the details of this idea each time it is invoked, resulting in a reduction of clutter and an easier time focusing on the larger issue, for which the thing being named is only one part. It has been our experience that to conquer coordinate space transformations, when communicating either to human beings via words or to computers via code, it is helpful to associate with each object a new coordinate space, which we call the upright coordinate space of the object. An object's upright space is, in a certain sense, “halfway” between world space and its object space. The axes of upright space are parallel with the axes of world space, but the origin of upright space is coincident with the origin of object space. Figure 3.2 illustrates this principle in 2D. (Notice that we have made an arbitrary choice to place the origin between the robot's feet, rather than at her center of mass.)
有时，正确的术语是更好地理解某个主题的关键。Don Knuth 创造了“命名并征服”（name and overcome）一词，指的是数学和计算机科学中一种常见且重要的实践，即为一个常用的概念命名。这样做的目的是避免每次调用时都重复该概念的细节，从而减少混乱，更容易集中精力于更大的问题，而命名的事物只是其中的一部分。根据我们的经验，为了克服坐标空间变换，无论是通过文字与人类沟通，还是通过代码与计算机沟通，为每个对象关联一个新的坐标空间都会很有帮助，我们称之为该对象的直立坐标空间。从某种意义上说，对象的直立空间位于世界空间和其对象空间的“中间”。直立空间的轴与世界空间的轴平行，但直立空间的原点与对象空间的原点重合。图 3.2 以二维形式展示了这一原理。 （请注意，我们任意选择将原点置于机器人的双脚之间，而不是其质心。）

Figure 3.2  图 3.2Object, upright, and world space.
物体、直立和世界空间。
Figure 3.3  图 3.3 Conversion between world and upright space via translation; upright and object space are related by rotation
通过平移在世界空间和直立空间之间进行转换；直立空间和物体空间通过旋转相互关联

Why is upright space interesting? To transform a point between object space and upright space requires only rotation, and to transform a point between upright space and world space requires only a change of location, which is usually called a translation. Thinking about these two things independently is easier than trying to cope with them both at once. This is shown in Figure 3.3. World space (on the left) is transformed into upright space (in the center) by translating the origin. To transform upright space into object space, we rotate the axes until they align with the object-space axes. In this example, the robot thinks that her y -axis points from her feet to her head and that her x -axis points to her left.3 We will return to this concept in Section 3.3.
为什么直立空间很有趣？在物体空间和直立空间之间变换一个点只需要旋转，在直立空间和世界空间之间变换一个点只需要改变位置，这通常称为平移。独立思考这两件事比试图同时处理它们更容易。如图 3.3 所示。通过平移原点，世界空间（左侧）转换为直立空间（中间）。要将直立空间转换为物体空间，我们旋转坐标轴，直到它们与物体空间坐标轴对齐。在这个例子中，机器人认为她的 y 轴从她的脚指向她的头部，而她的 x 轴指向她的左侧。3 我们将在第 3.3 节中回到这个概念。

The term “upright” is of our own invention and is not (yet!) a standard you are likely to find elsewhere. But it's a powerful concept in search of a good name. In physics, the term “center of mass coordinates” is sometimes used to describe coordinates expressed in the space that we are calling upright space. In the first edition of this book, we used the term “inertial space” to refer to this space, but we have changed it to avoid confusion with inertial reference frames in physics, which have some similar connotations but are different. We'll have a bit more philosophical pleas regarding upright space at the end of this chapter.
“直立”一词是我们自己发明的，（目前！）还未成为你在其他地方可能找到的标准。但它是一个强大的概念，正在寻求一个好名字。在物理学中，“质心坐标”有时用于描述我们称之为直立空间的空间中表达的坐标。在本书的第一版中，我们使用“惯性空间”来指代这个空间，但我们对其进行了修改，以避免与物理学中的惯性参考系混淆，它们有一些相似的含义，但有所不同。在本章末尾，我们将就直立空间提出更多哲学思考。

3.3Basis Vectors and Coordinate Space
Transformations
3.3 基向量和坐标空间变换

We said that a major justification for the existence of more than one coordinate space is because certain positions or directions are known only in a particular coordinate space. Likewise, sometimes certain questions can be answered only in particular coordinate spaces. When the question is best asked in one space, and the information we need in order to answer that question is known in a different space, we have a problem to solve.
我们说过，存在多个坐标空间的一个主要理由是，某些位置或方向仅在特定的坐标空间中已知。同样，有时某些问题也只能在特定的坐标空间中得到解答。当问题最好在一个坐标空间中提出，而我们解答该问题所需的信息在另一个坐标空间中已知时，我们就有了一个需要解决的问题。

For example, suppose that our robot is attempting to pick up a herring sandwich in our virtual world. We initially know the position of the sandwich and the position of the robot in world coordinates. World coordinates can be used to answer questions like “Is the sandwich north or south of me?” A different set of questions could be answered if we knew the position of the sandwich in the object space of the robot—for example, “Is the sandwich in front of me or behind me?” “Which way should I turn to face the sandwich?” “Which way do I move my herring sandwich scoop to get in position to pick up the sandwich?” Notice that to decide how to manipulate the gears and circuits, the object-space coordinates are the relevant ones. Furthermore, any data provided by sensors would be expressed in object space. Of course, our own bodies work under similar principles. All of us are capable of seeing a tasty morsel in front of us and putting it into our mouths without knowing which direction is “north.” (And thank goodness, too, or many of us would starve to death.)
例如，假设我们的机器人试图在虚拟世界中拾取一个鲱鱼三明治。我们最初知道三明治的位置以及机器人在世界坐标系中的位置。世界坐标可以用来回答诸如“三明治在我北边还是南边？”之类的问题。如果我们知道三明治在机器人物体空间中的位置，就可以回答一系列不同的问题——例如，“三明治在我前面还是在我后面？”“我应该转向哪个方向才能面向三明治？”“我应该把鲱鱼三明治勺移到哪个方向才能拾取三明治？”请注意，在决定如何操纵齿轮和电路时，物体空间坐标是相关的。此外，传感器提供的任何数据都将在物体空间中表示。当然，我们自己的身体也遵循类似的原理。我们所有人都能看到眼前美味的食物，并将其放入口中，而不知道哪个方向是“北”。（谢天谢地，否则我们中的许多人都会饿死。）

Further, suppose that we wish to render an image of the robot picking up the sandwich, and that the scene is illuminated by the light mounted on her shoulder. We know the position of the light within the robot's object space, but to properly light the scene, we must know the position of the light in world space.
进一步，假设我们希望渲染机器人拿起三明治的图像，并且场景由安装在机器人肩膀上的光源照亮。我们知道光源在机器人物体空间中的位置，但为了正确地照亮场景，我们必须知道光源在世界空间中的位置。

These problems are two sides of the same coin: we know how to express a point in one coordinate space, and we need to express that point in some other coordinate space. The technical term for this computation is a coordinate space transformation. We need to transform the position from world space to object space (in the example of the sandwich) or from object space to world space (in the example of the light). Notice that in this example, neither the sandwich nor the light really move, we are just expressing their locations in a different coordinate space.
这些问题如同一枚硬币的两面：我们知道如何在一个坐标空间中表达一个点，但我们需要在另一个坐标空间中表达这个点。这种计算的专业术语是坐标空间变换。我们需要将位置从世界空间变换到物体空间（以三明治为例），或者从物体空间变换到世界空间（以光为例）。请注意，在这个例子中，三明治和光实际上都没有移动，我们只是在不同的坐标空间中表达它们的位置。

The remainder of this section describes how to perform coordinate space transformations. Because this topic has such fundamental importance, and it can be so darn confusing, please allow us to present a very gradual transition from the warm fluffy high level to the cold hard math. Section 3.3.1 considers transformations in the very context they are often encountered for beginning video game programmers: graphics. Using the most ridiculous example we could think of, we show the basic need of transformations, and also demonstrate the duality between two useful ways of visualizing transformations. Section 3.3.2 makes sure we are clear about what it means to specify a coordinate space in terms of another space. Finally, Section 3.3.3 presents the key idea of basis vectors.
本节的剩余部分将介绍如何执行坐标空间变换。由于这个主题至关重要，而且可能非常令人困惑，请允许我们以非常渐进的方式，从温暖易懂的高级知识过渡到冰冷难懂的数学知识。第 3.3.1 节探讨了变换在初级电子游戏程序员经常遇到的环境中的应用：图形。我们使用一个我们能想到的最滑稽的例子，展示了变换的基本需求，并论证了两种可视化变换的实用方法之间的对偶性。第 3.3.2 节确保我们清楚地理解用另一个空间来指定一个坐标空间的含义。最后，第 3.3.3 节介绍了基向量的核心概念。

3.3.1Dual Perspectives  3.3.1 双重视角

In our robot example, the discussion was phrased in a way such that the process of transforming a point didn't really “move” the point, we just changed our frame of reference and were able to describe the point using a different coordinate space. In fact, you might say that we really didn't transform the point, we transformed the coordinate space! But there's another way of looking at coordinate space transformations. Some people find it easier in certain situations to imagine the coordinate space staying still while the point moves from one place to another. When we develop the math for actually calculating these transformations, this is the paradigm that is more natural. Coordinate space transforms are such an important tool, and the confusion that can arise because of an incomplete awareness of these two perspectives is so common that we will take a little bit of extra space to work through some examples.
在我们的机器人示例中，讨论的表述方式是，变换一个点的过程实际上并没有“移动”这个点，我们只是改变了参考系，并能够使用不同的坐标空间来描述这个点。事实上，你可能会说我们实际上并没有变换这个点，我们变换了坐标空间！但是，还有另一种看待坐标空间变换的方式。有些人在某些情况下更容易想象坐标空间保持不变，而点从一个位置移动到另一个位置。当我们开发用于实际计算这些变换的数学时，这种范式更为自然。坐标空间变换是一个非常重要的工具，由于对这两个视角的认识不完全而可能产生的混淆非常常见，因此我们将花一点额外的篇幅来解释一些示例。

Now for that ridiculous example. Let's say that we are working for a advertising agency that has just landed a big account with a food manufacturer. We are assigned to the project to make a slick computer-generated ad promoting one of their most popular items, Herring Packets, which are microwaveable herring food products for robots.
现在来看那个荒谬的例子。假设我们在一家广告公司工作，这家公司刚刚拿下一家食品制造商的大客户。我们被分配到这个项目，制作一则精妙的电脑生成广告，宣传他们最受欢迎的产品之一——鲱鱼包，这是一种机器人可微波加热的鲱鱼食品。

Figure 3.4  图 3.4 One serving contains 100%of a robot's recommended daily allowance of essential oils.
一份含有机器人每日推荐精油摄入量的 100%。

Of course, the client has a tendency to want changes made at the last minute, so we might need models of the product and robot in all possible positions and orientations. Our first attempt to accomplish this is to request, from the art department, the robot model and the product model in every possible configuration of positions and orientations. Unfortunately, they estimate that since this is an infinite amount, it will take all of eternity to produce this many assets, even after factoring in Moore's law and the fact that the product model is just a box. The director suggests increasing the art staff in order to achieve her vision, but unfortunately, after crunching the numbers, the producer discovers that this doesn't decrease the time required to finish the project.4 In fact, the company can afford resources to produce only one robot model and one box of microwaveable herring food product.
当然，客户往往希望在最后一刻做出更改，因此我们可能需要产品和机器人模型的所有可能位置和方向。为了实现此目标，我们首先尝试向艺术部门索取机器人模型和产品模型的所有可能位置和方向配置。不幸的是，他们估计由于这个数字是无限的，所以即使考虑到摩尔定律和产品模型只是一个盒子的事实，生产这么多资产也将需要永远的时间。总监建议增加艺术人员以实现她的愿景，但不幸的是，在计算了数字之后，制片人发现这并没有减少完成项目所需的时间。4 事实上，该公司只能提供生产一个机器人模型和一盒微波炉鲱鱼食品的资源。

Although you may regret spending the past 60 seconds of your life reading the preceding paragraph, this example does illustrate the fundamental necessity of coordinate space transformations. It's also a relatively accurate depiction of the creative process. Time estimates are always padded, project managers will throw more people at a project in desperation, projects must be done by a certain date to meet a quarter, and, most pertinent to this book, artists will deliver only one model, leaving it up to us to move it around in the world.
虽然你可能会后悔花了 60 秒阅读上一段，但这个例子确实说明了坐标空间变换的基本必要性。它也相对准确地描述了创作过程。时间估算总是被夸大，项目经理会迫于无奈而增加人手，项目必须在特定日期前完成才能满足季度目标，而且，与本书最相关的是，艺术家只会交付一个模型，而我们则需要自己去在世界各地移动它。

The 3D model we get from the artist is a mathematical representation of a robot. This description likely includes control points, called vertices, and some sort of surface description, which tells how to connect the vertices together to form the surface of the object. Depending on what tools were used by the artist to create the model, the surface description might be a polygon mesh or a subdivision surface. We're not too concerned about the surface description here; what's important is that we can move the model around by moving its vertices around. Let's ignore for now the fact that the robot is an articulated creature, and assume we can only move it around in the world like a chess piece, but not animate it.
我们从艺术家那里获得的 3D 模型是机器人的数学表示。这种描述可能包含控制点（称为顶点）以及某种表面描述，后者指示如何连接顶点以形成物体的表面。根据艺术家创建模型所使用的工具，表面描述可能是多边形网格或细分曲面。我们在这里不太关心表面描述；重要的是，我们可以通过移动顶点来移动模型。现在，我们先忽略机器人是关节生物的事实，假设我们只能像移动棋子一样在世界中移动它，而不能为其制作动画。

The artist who built our robot model decided (quite reasonably) to create her at the origin of the world space. This is depicted in Figure 3.5.
构建我们机器人模型的艺术家决定（相当合理地）将她创建在世界空间的原点。如图 3.5 所示。

Figure 3.5  图 3.5 The robot model was created with the world origin at her feet.
机器人模型是以她脚下的世界原点为基础而创建的。

To simplify the rest of this example, we're going to look at things from above. Although this is basically a 2D example, we're going to use our 3D conventions, ignoring the y -axis for now. In this book the convention is for +z to point “forward” in object space and “north” in upright space, whereas +x points “right” in object space and “east” in upright space.
为了简化本例的其余部分，我们将从上方观察。虽然这基本上是一个二维示例，但我们将使用三维约定，暂时忽略 y 轴。本书中的约定是 +z 在物体空间中指向“前方”，在垂直空间中指向“北”，而 +x 在物体空间中指向“右方”，在垂直空间中指向“东方”。

Figure 3.6  图 3.6Moving the model into position
将模型移动到位

For now, because the model is in its home position, object space and world space (and upright space) are all the same by definition. For all practical purposes, in the scene that the artist built containing only the model of the robot, world space is object space.
目前，由于模型处于其原始位置，物体空间和世界空间（以及直立空间）的定义相同。实际上，在艺术家构建的仅包含机器人模型的场景中，世界空间即为物体空间。

Original  原来的
position  位置
Step 1.  步骤 1.
Rotate  旋转
Step 2.  第 2 步。
Translate  翻译
Figure 3.7  图 3.7Transforming the robot from object space to world space by rotating, then translating
通过旋转，然后平移，将机器人从物体空间转换到世界空间

Back to advertising. Our goal is to transform the vertices of the model from their “home” location to some new location (in our case, into a make-believe kitchen), according to the desired position and orientation of the robot based on the executive whims at that moment, as shown in Figure 3.6.
回到广告话题。我们的目标是根据机器人当时的执行需求，将模型的顶点从其“原点”位置转换到某个新位置（在我们的例子中，是一个虚拟的厨房），如图 3.6 所示。

Let's talk a bit about how to accomplish this. We won't get too far into the mathematical details—that's what the rest of this chapter is for. Conceptually, to move the robot into position we first rotate her clockwise 120 o (or, as we'll learn in Section 8.3, by “heading left 120 o ”). Then we translate 18 ft east and 10 ft north, which according, to our conventions, is a 3D displacement of [18,0,10] . This is shown in Figure 3.7.
我们来简单谈谈如何实现这一点。我们不会深入探讨数学细节——本章剩余内容将专门讨论数学细节。从概念上讲，要将机器人移动到位，我们首先将其顺时针旋转 120 o （或者，正如我们将在 8.3 节中学习的那样，“向左旋转 120 o ”）。然后，我们向东平移 18 英尺，向北平移 10 英尺，根据我们的惯例，这相当于 3D 位移 [18,0,10] 。如图 3.7 所示。

At this time, please allow us a brief digression to answer a question that some readers may be asking: “Do we have to rotate first, and then translate?” The answer to this question is basically “yes.” Although it may seem more natural to translate before rotating, it's usually easier to rotate first. Here's why. When we rotate the object first, the center of rotation is the origin. Rotation about the origin and translation are two primitive tools we have at our disposal, and each is easy. (Recall our motivation for introducing upright space in Section 3.2.4.) If we rotate second, then that rotation will occur about a point that is not the origin. Rotation about the origin is a linear transform, but rotation about any other point is an affine transform. As we show in Section 6.4.3, to perform an affine transformation, we compose a sequence of primitive operations. For rotation about an arbitrary point, we translate the center of rotation to the origin, rotate about the origin, and then translate back. In other words, if we want to move the robot into place by translating first and rotating second, we likely go through the followingprocess:
现在，请允许我们稍微离题一下，回答一些读者可能会问的一个问题：“我们必须先旋转，然后再平移吗？” 这个问题的答案基本上是“是”。虽然先平移再旋转似乎更自然，但通常先旋转更容易。原因如下：当我们首先旋转物体时，旋转中心就是原点。绕原点旋转和平移是我们可以使用的两个基本工具，而且每个都很容易。（回想一下我们在 3.2.4 节中引入直立空间的动机。）如果我们第二个旋转，那么该旋转将围绕原点以外的点进行。绕原点旋转是线性变换，但绕任何其他点旋转都是仿射变换。如我们在 6.4.3 节中所示，要执行仿射变换，我们需要编写一系列基本操作。对于绕任意点旋转，我们将旋转中心平移到原点，绕原点旋转，然后再平移回来。换句话说，如果我们想先平移再旋转来将机器人移动到位，我们可能会经历以下过程：

Translating first and then rotating
先平移，后旋转
  1. Translate.   翻译。
  2. Rotate. Because we're rotating about a point that's not the origin, this is a three step process:
    旋转。因为我们旋转的点不是原点，所以这个过程分为三个步骤：
    1. a.Translate the center of rotation to the origin. (This undoes step 1.)
      a. 将旋转中心平移至原点。（此操作将撤销步骤 1。）
    2. b.Perform the rotation about the origin.
      b.绕原点旋转。
    3. c.Translate to put the center of rotation in place.
      c.平移以将旋转中心放置到位。

Notice that steps 1 and 2a cancel each other out, and we're left with the two steps: rotate first, then translate.
请注意，步骤 1 和 2a 相互抵消，我们只剩下两个步骤：先旋转，然后平移。

Overhead view  俯视图 Camera's view  相机视图
Figure 3.8  图 3.8The layout of the camera and robot in the scene
场景中摄像机和机器人的布局

So we've managed to get the robot model into the right place in the world. But to render it, we need to transform the vertices of the model into camera space. In other words, we need to express the coordinates of the vertices relative to the camera. For example, if a vertex is 9 ft in front of the camera and 3 ft to the right, then the z - and x -coordinates of that vertex in camera space would be 9 and 3, respectively. Figure 3.8 shows a particular shot we might want to capture. On the left, we see the layout of the shot from an external perspective, and on the right is what the camera sees.
这样，我们就能将机器人模型放置到现实世界的正确位置。但要渲染它，我们需要将模型的顶点变换到相机空间。换句话说，我们需要表达顶点相对于相机的坐标。例如，如果一个顶点位于相机前方 9 英尺处，右侧 3 英尺处，那么该顶点在相机空间中的 z 和 x 坐标分别为 9 和 3。图 3.8 展示了我们可能想要捕捉的一个特定镜头。左侧是从外部视角看到的镜头布局，右侧是相机所见的画面。

It was easy to visualize transforming the model into world space. We literally “moved” it into place.5 But how do we transform from world space to camera space? The objects are both already “in place,” so where do we “move” them? For situations like this, it's helpful to think about transforming the coordinate space rather than transforming the objects, a technique we'll discuss in the next section. However, let's see if we can keep the coordinate space stationary, and still achieve the desired result by only “moving objects.”
将模型变换到世界空间的过程很容易想象。我们实际上是把它“移动”到位了。5 但是，如何从世界空间变换到相机空间呢？物体都已经“就位”了，那么我们该把它们“移动”到哪里呢？对于这种情况，考虑变换坐标空间而不是变换物体会更有帮助，我们将在下一节讨论这项技术。但是，让我们看看是否可以保持坐标空间不变，同时仍然通过“移动物体”来实现预期的效果。

When we transformed from object space to world space, we were able to do so because we imagined the robot starting out at the origin in world space. Of course, the robot never really was at the location in world space, but we imagined it. Since we transformed from object space to world space by moving the object, perhaps we can transform from world space to camera space by moving the world! Imagine taking the entire world, including the robot, the camera, and the kitchen, and moving everything around. Clearly, such operations wouldn't affect what the camera would “see,” because they don't change the relative relationship between the camera and the objects in the world. If we moved the world and camera together, such that the camera moved to the origin, then world-space coordinates and camera-space coordinates would be the same. Figure 3.9 shows the two-step process that we would use to achieve this.
当我们从物体空间变换到世界空间时，我们之所以能够做到这一点，是因为我们想象机器人从世界空间的原点出发。当然，机器人实际上从未位于世界空间的该位置，只是我们想象了它而已。既然我们通过移动物体实现了从物体空间到世界空间的变换，那么或许我们可以通过移动世界空间来实现从世界空间到相机空间的变换！想象一下，将整个世界空间，包括机器人、相机和厨房，全部移动。显然，这样的操作不会影响相机“看到”的内容，因为它们不会改变相机与世界中物体之间的相对关系。如果我们同时移动世界空间和相机空间，使相机移动到原点，那么世界空间坐标和相机空间坐标将相同。图 3.9 展示了我们实现此目标的两步过程。

Original  原来的
position  位置
Step 1.  步骤 1.
Translate  翻译
Step 2.  第 2 步。
Rotate  旋转
Figure 3.9  图 3.9Transforming everything from world space to camera space by translating, then rotating
通过平移、旋转将一切从世界空间转换到相机空间

Notice that, in this case, it's easier to translate before rotating. That's because we want to rotate about the origin. Also, we use the opposite translation and rotation amounts, compared to the camera's position and orientation. For example, in Figure 3.9 the coordinates of the camera are approximately (13.5,4,2) . (The grid lines represent 10 units.) So to move the camera to the origin, we translate everything by [−13.5,−4,−2] . The camera is facing roughly northeast and thus has a clockwise heading compared to north; a counterclockwise rotation is required to align camera-space axes with the world-space axes.
请注意，在这种情况下，先平移再旋转更容易。这是因为我们想要绕原点旋转。此外，与相机的位置和方向相比，我们使用了相反的平移和旋转量。例如，在图 3.9 中，相机的坐标约为 (13.5,4,2) 。（网格线代表 10 个单位。）因此，要将相机移动到原点，我们需要将所有内容平移 [−13.5,−4,−2] 。相机大致面向东北，因此相对于北方，其航向为顺时针；需要逆时针旋转以使相机空间轴与世界空间轴对齐。

After picking up and moving around an entire robot in the first step, and then the entire world6 in the second step, we finally have the coordinates of the vertices in camera space, and can proceed with rendering. If all this imaginary heavy lifting has worn you out, don't worry; in just a moment we will discuss an alternate way to think about this process.
在第一步拾取并移动整个机器人，然后在第二步移动整个世界 6 之后，我们终于得到了相机空间中顶点的坐标，可以继续进行渲染了。如果所有这些想象中的繁重工作让您感到疲惫不堪，别担心；稍后我们将讨论另一种思考这个过程的方式。

Before we move on, a few important notes about this example. First, the world-to-camera transform is usually done in a vertex shader; you can leave this to the graphics API if you are working at a high level and not writing your own shaders. Second, camera space isn't the “finish line” as far as the graphics pipeline is concerned. From camera space, vertices are transformed into clip space and finally projected to screen space. These details are covered in Section 10.2.3.
在继续之前，先来了解一下这个例子的一些重要信息。首先，世界空间到相机空间的变换通常在顶点着色器中完成；如果您在高层工作，并且不编写自己的着色器，则可以将此交给图形 API 来完成。其次，就图形管线而言，相机空间并非“终点线”。顶点会从相机空间变换到裁剪空间，最终投影到屏幕空间。这些细节将在 10.2.3 节中介绍。

Absolute perspective  绝对视角 Local perspective  当地视角
Robot  机器人
object  目的
space  空间
Robot  机器人
upright  直立
space  空间
World  世界
space  空间
Camera  相机
upright  直立
space  空间
Camera  相机
space  空间
Figure 3.10  图 3.10 The same sequence of coordinate space transformations is viewed from two perspectives. On the left, it appears as if the objects are moving, and the coordinate axes are stationary. On the right, the objects appear to be stationary, and the coordinate space axes are transformed.
从两个角度观察相同的坐标空间变换序列。左侧视图中，物体看起来好像在移动，而坐标轴静止不动。右侧视图中，物体看起来静止不动，而坐标空间轴发生了变换。

So we've seen how we can compute world-space coordinates from object-space coordinates by imagining moving the model from the origin to its position in the world. Then we could compute camera-space coordinates from world-space coordinates by shifting the entire world to put the camera at the origin. The point to emphasize is that the coordinate space used to describe the points remained constant (even if we called it different names at different times), while we imaged the points moving in space. A transformation thus interpreted is sometimes called an active transformation.
我们已经了解了如何通过想象将模型从原点移动到其在世界中的位置，从而根据物体空间坐标计算世界空间坐标。然后，我们可以通过移动整个世界，将相机置于原点，从而根据世界空间坐标计算相机空间坐标。需要强调的是，当我们想象点在空间中移动时，用于描述点的坐标空间保持不变（即使我们在不同时间对其有不同的称呼）。这样解释的变换有时被称为主动变换。

Alternatively, we can think of the same process as a passive transformation. In the passive paradigm, we imagine the points being stationary while we move the coordinate space used to describe those points. In either case, the coordinates of the points are the same at each step. It's all in how we choose to view the situation. Earlier, our perspective was fixed with the coordinate space, because we were thinking of the transformation in active terms. Now we show the dual perspective, which is fixed relative to the object.
或者，我们可以将同一过程视为被动变换。在被动范式中，我们假设点是静止的，而我们移动的是描述这些点的坐标空间。无论哪种情况，点的坐标在每一步都是相同的。这完全取决于我们如何看待情况。之前，我们的视角是固定在坐标空间中的，因为我们是从主动的角度来思考变换的。现在我们展示的是相对于物体固定的对偶视角。

Figure 3.10 reviews the four-step sequence from the robot's object space to the camera's object space from both perspectives. On the left, we repeat the presentation just given, where the coordinate space is stationary and the robot is moving around. On the right, we show the same process as a passive transformation, from a perspective that remains fixed relative to the robot. Notice how the coordinate space appears to move around. Also, notice that when we perform a certain transformation to the vertices, it's equivalent to performing the opposite transformation to the coordinate space. The duality between active and passive transformations is a frequent a source of confusion. Always make sure when you are turning some transformation into math (or code), to be clear in your mind whether the object or the coordinate space is being transformed. We consider a classic example of this confusion from graphics in Section 8.7.1, when we discuss how to convert Euler angles to the corresponding rotation matrix.
图 3.10 从两个视角回顾了从机器人的物体空间到相机的物体空间的四步序列。左侧，我们重复刚才的演示，其中坐标空间静止，而机器人在移动。右侧，我们以被动变换的形式展示了相同的过程，但视角相对于机器人保持不变。请注意坐标空间是如何移动的。另外，请注意，当我们对顶点执行某种变换时，它相当于对坐标空间执行相反的变换。主动变换和被动变换之间的对偶性经常引起混淆。在将某些变换转换为数学（或代码）时，务必确保清楚变换的是对象还是坐标空间。我们将在 8.7.1 节中讨论如何将欧拉角转换为相应的旋转矩阵时，从图形学的角度来考虑这种混淆的一个典型示例。

Note that for clarity, the first two rows in Figure 3.10 have the kitchen and camera mostly transparent. In reality, each individual object—the pots, the refrigerator, and so on—could have been made by an artist at the center of some scene, and conceptually each undergoes its own unique transform from object space to world space.
请注意，为了清晰起见，图 3.10 中的前两行将厨房和摄像机几乎透明化。实际上，每个单独的物体——锅、冰箱等等——都可以由艺术家在某个场景的中心制作，并且从概念上讲，每个物体都会经历从物体空间到世界空间的独特变换。

We discussed two useful ways of imagining coordinate space transformations. One way is to fix our perspective with the coordinate space. This is the active transformation paradigm: the vectors and objects move around as their coordinates change. In the passive transformation paradigm, we keep our perspective fixed relative to the thing being transformed, making it appear as if we are transforming the coordinate space used to measure the coordinates. Transforming an object has the same effect on the coordinates as performing the opposite transformation to the coordinate space. Both the active and passive paradigms are quite useful, and an inadequate appreciation of the difference between them is a common cause of mistakes.
我们讨论了两种想象坐标空间变换的实用方法。一种方法是将视角与坐标空间固定。这被称为主动变换范式：向量和物体随着其坐标的变化而移动。在被动变换范式中，我们保持视角相对于被变换物体的固定，使其看起来就像是在变换用于测量坐标的坐标空间。变换一个物体对坐标的影响与对坐标空间执行相反的变换相同。主动和被动范式都非常有用，但对它们之间的区别理解不足是导致错误的常见原因。

3.3.2Specifying Coordinate Spaces
3.3.2 指定坐标空间

We are almost ready to talk about transformations. But there's actually one more basic question we should answer first: exactly how do we specify a coordinate space relative to another coordinate space?7 Recall from Section 1.2.2 that a coordinate system is defined by its origin and axes. The origin defines the position of the coordinate space, and the axes describe its orientation. (Actually, the axes can describe other information, such as scale and skew. For the moment, we assume that the axes are perpendicular and the units used by the axes are the same as the units used by the parent coordinate space.) So if we can find a way to describe the origin and the axes, then we have fully documented the coordinate space.
我们差不多可以开始讨论变换了。但实际上，我们首先应该回答一个更基本的问题：我们究竟如何指定一个坐标空间相对于另一个坐标空间的位置？7 回想一下 1.2.2 节，坐标系由其原点和轴定义。原点定义了坐标空间的位置，轴描述了其方向。（实际上，轴可以描述其他信息，例如缩放和倾斜。目前，我们假设轴是垂直的，并且轴使用的单位与父坐标空间使用的单位相同。）因此，如果我们能找到一种方法来描述原点和轴，那么我们就完整地记录了坐标空间。

Specifying the position of the coordinate space is straightforward. All we have to do is describe the location of the origin. We do this just like we do for any other point. Of course, we must express this point relative to the parent coordinate space, not the local child space. The origin of the child space, by definition, is always (0,0,0) when expressed in child coordinate space. For example, consider the position of the 2D robot in Figure 3.2. To establish a scale for the diagram, let's say the robot is around 5 1/2 feet tall. Then the world-space coordinates of her origin are close to (4.5,1.5) .
指定坐标空间的位置很简单。我们只需描述原点的位置即可。就像处理其他任何点一样。当然，我们必须相对于父坐标空间而不是本地子空间来表示此点。根据定义，子空间的原点在子坐标空间中始终为 (0,0,0) 。例如，考虑图 3.2 中二维机器人的位置。为了确定该图的比例，我们假设机器人大约 5.5 英尺高。那么，其原点的世界空间坐标接近 (4.5,1.5) 。

Specifying the orientation of a coordinate space in 3D is only slightly more complicated. The axes are vectors (directions), and can be specified like any other direction vector. Going back to our robot example, we could describe her orientation by telling what directions the green vectors labeled +x and +y were pointing—these are the axes of the robot's object space. (Actually, we would use vectors with unit length. The axes in the diagrams were drawn as large as possible, but, as we see in just a moment, unit vectors are usually used to describe the axes.) Just as with position, we do not use the object space itself to describe the object-space axis directions, since those coordinates are [1,0] and [0,1] by definition. Instead, the coordinates are specified in upright space. In this example, unit vectors in the +x and +y object-space directions have upright-space coordinates of [0.87,0.50] and [−0.50,0.87] , respectively.
在 3D 中指定坐标空间的方向仅稍微复杂一些。轴是向量（方向），可以像任何其他方向向量一样指定。回到我们的机器人示例，我们可以通过标有 +x 和 +y 的绿色向量指向的方向来描述她的方向——这些是机器人物体空间的轴。（实际上，我们会使用单位长度的向量。图中的轴画得尽可能大，但正如我们马上会看到的，通常使用单位向量来描述轴。）与位置一样，我们不使用物体空间本身来描述物体空间轴方向，因为根据定义，这些坐标是 [1,0] 和 [0,1] 。相反，坐标是在直立空间中指定的。在此示例中，物体空间方向 +x 和 +y 的单位向量分别具有直立空间坐标 [0.87,0.50] 和 [−0.50,0.87] 。

What we have just described is one way to specify the orientation of a coordinate space, but there are others. For example, in 2D, rather than listing two 2D vectors, we could give a single angle. (The robot's object axes are rotated clockwise 30 o relative to the upright axes.) In 3D, describing orientation is considerably more complicated, and in fact we have devoted all of Chapter 8 to the subject.
我们刚才描述的是指定坐标空间方向的一种方法，但还有其他方法。例如，在二维空间中，我们可以给出一个角度，而不是列出两个二维向量。（机器人的物体轴相对于直立轴顺时针旋转 30 o 。）在三维空间中，描述方向要复杂得多，事实上，我们已经用第 8 章的全部内容来讨论这个主题。

We specify a coordinate space by describing its origin and axes. The origin is a point that defines the position of the space and can be described just like any other point. The axes are vectors and describe the orientation of the space (and possibly other information such as scale), and the usual tools for describing vectors can be used. The coordinates we use to measure the origin and axes must be relative to some other coordinate space.
我们通过描述坐标空间的原点和轴来指定它。原点是定义空间位置的点，可以像描述其他点一样进行描述。轴是向量，描述空间的方向（可能还有其他信息，例如比例），可以使用描述向量的常用工具。我们用来测量原点和轴的坐标必须相对于其他坐标空间。

3.3.3Basis Vectors  3.3.3 基础向量

Now we are ready to actually compute some coordinate space transforms. We start with a concrete 2D example. Let's say that we need to know the world-space coordinates of the light that is attached to the robot's right shoulder. We start with the object-space coordinates, which are (−1,5) . How do we get the world-space coordinates? To do this, we must go back to the beginning and poke deeper into some ideas that are so fundamental as to be taken for granted. How do we locate a point indicated by a given set of Cartesian coordinates? Let's say we needed to give step-by-step directions for how to locate the light to somebody who didn't know how Cartesian coordinates worked. We would say:
现在我们准备实际计算一些坐标空间变换。我们从一个具体的二维示例开始。假设我们需要知道机器人右肩上安装的光源的世界空间坐标。我们从物体空间坐标开始，即 (−1,5) 。如何获取世界空间坐标？为此，我们必须回到最初，深入探究一些基础到理所当然的概念。如何定位给定一组笛卡尔坐标所指示的点？假设我们需要向不了解笛卡尔坐标系工作原理的人逐步指导如何定位光源。我们会说：

  1. Start at the origin.
    从原点开始。
  2. Move to the right 1 foot.
    向右移动 1 英尺。
  3. Move up 5 feet.   向上移动 5 英尺。

We assume this person has a tape measure, and understands that when we say “right” and “up,” we mean the robot's “right” and “up,” the directions that we enlightened people know as being parallel to the object-space axes.
我们假设这个人有一把卷尺，并且明白当我们说“右”和“上”时，我们指的是机器人的“右”和“上”，也就是我们开明的人所知道的与物体空间轴平行的方向。

Now here's the key point: we already know how to describe the origin, the direction called “the robot's right,” and the direction called “the robot's up” in world coordinates! They are part of the specification of the coordinate space, which we just gave in the previous section. So all we have to do is follow our own instructions, and at each step, keep track of the world-space coordinates. Examine Figure 3.2 again.
现在关键点来了：我们已经知道如何在世界坐标系中描述原点、“机器人右侧”方向以及“机器人上方”方向！它们是坐标空间规范的一部分，我们在上一节中已经给出。所以我们要做的就是按照我们自己的指示，在每一步中跟踪世界空间坐标。再次检查图 3.2。

  1. Start at the origin. No problem, we previously determined that her origin was at
    从原点开始。没问题，我们之前确定她的原点是
    (4.5,1.5).
  2. Move to the right 1 foot. We know that the vector “the robot's left” is [0.87,0.50] , and so we scale this direction by the distance of −1 unit, and add on the displacement to our position, to get
    向右移动 1 英尺。我们知道“机器人左侧”的向量是 [0.87,0.50] ，因此我们将此方向缩放 −1 个单位的距离，并将位移添加到我们的位置，得到
    (4.5,1.5)+(−1)×[0.87,0.50]=(3.63,1).
  3. Move up 5 feet. Once again, we know that “the robot's up” direction is [−0.50,0.87] , so we just scale this by 5 units and add it to the result, yielding
    向上移动 5 英尺。同样，我们知道“机器人向上”的方向是 [−0.50,0.87] ，所以我们只需将其缩放 5 个单位，然后将其添加到结果中，得到
    (4.5,1.5)+(−1)×[0.87,0.50]+5×[−0.50,0.87]=(1.13,5.35).

If you look again at Figure 3.2, you'll see that, indeed, the world-space coordinates of the light are approximately (1.13,5.35) .
如果你再看一下图 3.2，你就会发现，光的世界空间坐标确实大约为 (1.13,5.35) 。

Now let's remove the numbers specific to this example, and make some more abstract statements. Let b be some arbitrary point whose body-space coordinates b =(bx,by) are known. Let w =(wx,wy) represent the world-space coordinates of that same point. We know the world-space coordinates for the origin o and the left and up directions, which we denote as p and q , respectively. Now w can be computed by
现在，让我们移除此示例特有的数字，并进行一些更抽象的陈述。令 b 为某个任意点，其身体空间坐标 b =(bx,by) 已知。令 w =(wx,wy) 表示同一点的世界空间坐标。我们知道原点 o 以及向左和向上方向的世界空间坐标，分别表示为 p 和 q 。现在，可以通过以下方式计算 w

(3.1) w = o +bx p +by q .

Now let's be even more general. In order to do so, it will help greatly to remove translation from our consideration. One way to do this is to discard “points” and think exclusively of vectors, which, as geometric entities, do not have a position (only magnitude and direction); thus translation does not really have a meaning for them. Alternatively, we can simply restrict the object space origin to be the same as the world-space origin.
现在让我们更概括地讨论。为了做到这一点，将平移从我们的考虑中移除将大有帮助。一种方法是抛弃“点”，只考虑向量。向量作为几何实体，没有位置（只有大小和方向）；因此平移对它们来说实际上没有任何意义。或者，我们可以简单地将对象空间原点限制为与世界空间原点相同。

Remember that in Section 2.3.1 we discussed how any vector may be decomposed geometrically into a sequence of axially-aligned displacements. Thus, an arbitrary vector v can be written in “expanded” form as
记得在 2.3.1 节中，我们讨论了如何将任意向量几何分解为一系列轴向对齐的位移。因此，任意向量 v 可以“展开”为

Expressing a 3D vector as a linear combination of basis vectors
将三维向量表示为基向量的线性组合
(3.2) v =x p +y q +z r .

Here, p , q , and r are basis vectors for 3D space. The vector v could have any possible magnitude and direction, and we could uniquely determine the coordinates x , y , z (unless p , q , and r are chosen poorly; we discuss this key point in just a moment). Equation (3.2) expresses v as a linear combination of the basis vectors.
这里， p 、 q 和 r 是三维空间的基向量。向量 v 可以具有任意大小和方向，并且我们可以唯一地确定坐标 x 、 y 、 z （除非 p 、 q 和 r 选择不当；我们稍后会讨论这个关键点）。方程 (3.2) 将 v 表示为基向量的线性组合。

Here is a common, but a bit incomplete, way to think about basis vectors: most of the time, p =[1,0,0] , q =[0,1,0] , and r =[0,0,1] ; in other unusual circumstances, p , q , and r have different coordinates. This is not quite right. When thinking about p , q , and r , we must distinguish between the vectors as geometric entities (earlier, p and q were the physical directions of “left” and “up”) and the particular coordinates used to describe those vectors. The former is inherently immutable; the latter depends on the choice of basis. Plenty of books emphasize this by defining all vectors in terms of the “world basis vectors,” which are often denoted i , j , and k and are interpreted as elemental geometric entities that cannot be further decomposed. They do not have “coordinates,” although certain axioms are taken to be true, such as i × j = k . In this framework, a coordinate triple [x,y,z] is a mathematical entity, which does not have a geometric meaning until we take the linear combination x i +y j +z k . Now, in response to the assertion i =[1,0,0] , we might argue that since i is a geometric entity, it cannot be compared against a mathematical object, in the same way that the equation “ kilometer =3.2 ” is nonsense. Because the letters i , j , and k carry this weighty elemental connotation, we instead use the less presumptuous symbols p , q , and r , and whenever we use these symbols to name our basis vectors, the message is: “we're using these as our basis vectors for now, but we might know how to express p , q , r relative to some other basis, so they aren't necessarily the `root' basis.”
这是一种常见但有点不完整的思考基向量的方式：大多数情况下， p =[1,0,0] 、 q =[0,1,0] 和 r =[0,0,1] ；在其他特殊情况下， p 、 q 和 r 具有不同的坐标。这并不完全正确。在思考 p 、 q 和 r 时，我们必须区分作为几何实体的向量（之前， p 和 q 是“左”和“上”的物理方向）和用于描述这些向量的特定坐标。前者本质上是不可变的；后者取决于基的选择。许多书籍通过根据“世界基向量”定义所有向量来强调这一点，这些基向量通常表示为 i 、 j 和 k 并被解释为无法进一步分解的基本几何实体。它们没有“坐标”，尽管某些公理被认为是正确的，例如 i × j = k 。在这个框架中，坐标三元组 [x,y,z] 是一个数学实体，在我们取线性组合 x i +y j +z k 之前，它不具有几何意义。现在，为了回应断言 i =[1,0,0] ，我们可能会争辩说，由于 i 是一个几何实体，它不能与数学对象进行比较，就像等式“ kilometer =3.2 ”是无稽之谈一样。由于字母 i 、 j 和 k 带有这种重要的基本内涵，我们改用不那么自以为是的符号 p 、 q 和 r ，每当我们使用这些符号来命名基向量时，传达的信息是：“我们现在使用这些作为基向量，但我们可能知道如何相对于其他基来表示 p 、 q 、 r ，所以它们不一定是‘根’基。”

The coordinates of p , q , and r are always equal to [1,0,0] , [0,1,0] , and [0,0,1] , respectively, when expressed using the coordinate space for which they are the basis, but relative to some other basis they will have arbitrary coordinates. When we say that we are using the standard basis, this is equivalent to saying that we are concerning ourselves with only a single coordinate space. What we call that coordinate space makes no difference, since we have no way to reference any other coordinate space without introducing basis vectors. When we do consider any alternative basis, we have implicitly introduced another coordinate space: the space used to measure the coordinates of the basis vectors!
当使用以它们为基的坐标空间表示时， p 、 q 和 r 的坐标始终分别等于 [1,0,0] 、 [0,1,0] 和 [0,0,1] ，但相对于其他基，它们将具有任意坐标。当我们说我们正在使用标准基时，这相当于说我们只关注一个坐标空间。我们称该坐标空间为无所谓，因为如果不引入基向量，我们就无法引用任何其他坐标空间。当我们考虑任何其他基时，我们已经隐式引入了另一个坐标空间：用于测量基向量坐标的空间！

The coordinates of basis vectors are measured in terms of a reference frame that is different from the one for which they are a basis. Thus basis vectors are intimately linked with coordinate space transformations.
基向量的坐标是根据与其基不同的参考系来测量的。因此，基向量与坐标空间变换密切相关。

We said earlier that p , q , and r could be chosen “poorly.” This begs the question: what makes a good basis? We are accustomed to having basis vectors that are mutually perpendicular. We are also used to them having the same length: we expect the displacements 5 p and 5 q to be in different directions, but we ordinarily would assume that they have the same length. Finally, when multiple coordinate spaces are involved, we are also used to them all having the same scale. That is, the vector v has the same numeric magnitude, no matter what coordinate system we use to measure it. But as we're about to see, that isn't necessarily the case. These properties are certainly desirable; in fact, we might say that this is the “best basis” in many cases. But they may not always be immediately available, they are often not necessary, and there are some situations for which we purposefully choose basis vectors without these properties.
我们之前说过， p 、 q 和 r 的选择可能“不太好”。这就引出了一个问题：什么样的基向量才是好的基向量？我们习惯于基向量相互垂直。我们也习惯于它们具有相同的长度：我们预期位移 5 p 和 5 q 的方向不同，但通常假设它们的长度相同。最后，当涉及多个坐标空间时，我们也习惯于它们都具有相同的尺度。也就是说，无论我们使用哪个坐标系来测量向量 v ，它都具有相同的数值幅值。但正如我们即将看到的，情况并非总是如此。这些属性当然是可取的；事实上，在很多情况下，我们可能会说这是“最佳基向量”。但它们并非总是立即可用，它们通常不是必需的，并且在某些情况下，我们会故意选择不具备这些属性的基向量。

We briefly mention here two examples, both from the world of graphics. Imagine we want to animate a squishing or stretching motion of our robot model. To do so, we would modify the coordinate space used to interpret the coordinates of our vertices. We would animate the basis vectors of the robot's object space, probably in ways that caused them to have different lengths from one another or to cease to be perpendicular. As we squish or stretch the object-space vectors, the object-space coordinates of the vertices remain constant, but the resulting camera-space coordinates change, producing the desired animation.
我们在这里简要提及两个图形领域的例子。假设我们想要为机器人模型制作一个挤压或拉伸的动画。为此，我们需要修改用于解释顶点坐标的坐标空间。我们需要对机器人对象空间的基向量进行动画处理，这可能会导致它们的长度彼此不同，或者不再垂直。当我们挤压或拉伸对象空间向量时，顶点的对象空间坐标保持不变，但由此产生的相机空间坐标会发生变化，从而产生所需的动画。

Another example arises with basis vectors for texture mapping. (We're getting a bit ahead of ourselves, since we won't talk about texture mapping until Section 10.5; however we are aware that our readers are not a tabula rasa, and we suspect you have at least heard of these concepts. We are also aware that many readers' first introduction to the term basis vector is in the context of bump mapping; hopefully this example will help place that particular usage of the term in the proper context.) It's often helpful to establish a local coordinate space on the surface of an object where one axis (we'll use +z ) is parallel to the surface normal, and the other axes point in the direction of increasing u and v in the texture. These latter two basis vectors are sometimes called the tangent and binormal. Motion in 3D space in the direction of the tangent basis vector corresponds to horizontal motion in the 2D image space of the texture, while a displacement in 3D space in the direction of the binormal would correspond to vertical image-space displacement. The key fact is that the flat 2D texture often must be warped to wrap it around an irregular surface, and the basis vectors are not guaranteed to be perpendicular.8
另一个例子是关于纹理映射的基向量。（我们有点超前了，因为我们直到 10.5 节才会讨论纹理映射；不过，我们知道读者并非一无所知，我们猜想你们至少听说过这些概念。我们也知道，许多读者第一次接触“基向量”这个术语是在凹凸贴图的语境中；希望这个例子能帮助读者理解这个术语的具体用法。）在物体表面建立一个局部坐标空间通常很有帮助，其中一个轴（我们将使用 +z ）平行于表面法线，其他轴指向纹理中 u 和 v 递增的方向。后两个基向量有时被称为切线和副法线。在三维空间中，沿切线基向量方向的运动对应于纹理二维图像空间中的水平运动，而在三维空间中，沿副法线方向的位移对应于图像空间中的垂直位移。关键事实是，平面二维纹理通常必须扭曲才能将其包裹在不规则表面上，并且基向量不能保证垂直。8

Figure 3.11  图 3.11Basis vectors don't have to be perpendicular.
基向量不必垂直。

Figure 3.11 shows a situation in which the basis vectors p and q have the same length, but are not perpendicular. Although we've shown only two example vectors, a and b , the set of vectors that can be described as a linear combination x p +y q fill an infinite plane, and for any vector in this plane, the coordinates [x,y] are uniquely determined.
图 3.11 展示了基向量 p 和 q 长度相等但不垂直的情况。虽然我们只展示了两个示例向量 a 和 b ，但可以描述为线性组合的向量集 x p +y q 填充了一个无限平面，并且对于该平面中的任何向量，其坐标 [x,y] 都是唯一确定的。

The set of vectors that can be expressed as a linear combination of the basis vectors is called the span of the basis. In the example in Figure 3.11, the span is an infinite 2D plane. This might seem at first like it's the only possible scenario, but let's examine some more interesting situations. First of all, note that we said that the vectors fill “an” infinite plane, not “the” plane. Just because we have two coordinates and basis vectors does not mean that p and q must be 2D vectors! They could be 3D vectors, in which case their span will be some arbitrary plane within 3D space, as depicted in Figure 3.12.
能够表示为基向量线性组合的向量集合称为基向量的跨度。在图 3.11 的示例中，跨度是一个无限的二维平面。乍一看，这似乎是唯一可能的情况，但让我们来研究一些更有趣的情况。首先，请注意，我们说的是向量填充“一个”无限平面，而不是“那个”平面。仅仅因为我们有两个坐标和基向量，并不意味着 p 和 q 一定是二维向量！它们可以是三维向量，在这种情况下，它们的跨度将是三维空间中的任意平面，如图 3.12 所示。

Figure 3.12  图 3.12 The two basis vectors p and q span a 2D subset of the 3D space.
两个基向量 p 和 q 跨越 3D 空间的 2D 子集。

Figure 3.12 illustrates several key points. Note that we have chosen a and b to have the same coordinates from Figure 3.11, at least relative to the basis vectors p and q . Second, when working within the space of p and q , our example vectors a and b are 2D vectors; they have only two coordinates, x and y . We might also be interested in their 3D “world” coordinates; these are obtained simply by expanding the linear combination x p +y q ; the result of this expression is a 3D vector.
图 3.12 阐明了几个关键点。注意，我们选择的 a 和 b 具有与图 3.11 相同的坐标，至少相对于基向量 p 和 q 而言。其次，在 p 和 q 的空间中，我们的示例向量 a 和 b 是二维向量；它们只有两个坐标： x 和 y 。我们可能也对它们的三维“世界”坐标感兴趣；这些坐标可以通过展开线性组合 x p +y q 获得；该表达式的结果是一个三维向量。

Consider the vector c , which lies behind the plane in Figure 3.12. This vector is not in the span of p and q , which means we cannot express it as a linear combination of the basis. In other words, there are no coordinates [cx,cy] such that c =cx p +cy q .
考虑向量 c ，它位于图 3.12 中的平面后方。该向量不在 p 和 q 的跨度内，这意味着我们不能将其表示为基的线性组合。换句话说，不存在坐标 [cx,cy] 使得 c =cx p +cy q 。

The term used to describe the number of dimensions in the space spanned by the basis is the rank of the basis. In both of the examples so far, we have two basis vectors that span a two-dimensional space. Clearly, if we have n basis vectors, the best we can hope for is full rank, meaning the span is an n -dimensional space. But is it possible for the rank to be less than n ? For example, if we have three basis vectors, is it possible that the span of those basis vectors is only 2D or 1D? The answer is “yes,” and this situation corresponds to what we meant earlier by a “poor choice” of basis vectors.
用来描述基所跨越空间维数的术语是基的秩。到目前为止的两个例子中，我们都有跨越二维空间的两个基向量。显然，如果我们有 n 个基向量，我们所能期望的最好结果是满秩，这意味着跨度是 n 维空间。但是，秩有可能小于 n 吗？例如，如果我们有三个基向量，这些基向量的跨度是否可能只有二维或一维？答案是肯定的，这种情况对应于我们之前所说的基向量“选择不当”。

For example, let's say we add a third basis vector r to our set p and q . If r lies in the span of p and q (for example, let's say we chose r = a or r = b as our third basis vector), then the basis vectors are linearly dependent, and do not have full rank. Adding in this last vector did not allow us to describe any vectors that could not already be described with just p and q . Furthermore, now the coordinates [x,y,z] for a given vector in the span of the basis are not uniquely determined. The basis vectors span a space with only two degrees of freedom, but we have three coordinates. The blame doesn't fall on r in particular, he just happened to be the new guy. We could have chosen any pair of vectors from p , q , a , and b , as a valid basis for this same space. The problem of linear dependence is a problem with the set as a whole, not just one particular vector. In contrast, if our third basis vector was chosen to be any other vector that didn't lie in the plane spanned by p and q (for example, the vector c ), then the basis would be linearly independent and have full rank. If a set of basis vectors are linearly independent, then it is not possible to express any one basis vector as a linear combination of the others.
例如，假设我们在集合 p 和 q 中添加第三个基向量 r 。如果 r 位于 p 和 q 的范围内（例如，假设我们选择 r = a 或 r = b 作为第三个基向量），则基向量是线性相关的，并且不是满秩的。添加最后一个向量不允许我们描述任何不能用 p 和 q 描述的向量。此外，现在基跨度内给定向量的坐标 [x,y,z] 不是唯一确定的。基向量跨越只有两个自由度的空间，但我们有三个坐标。责任并不特别落在 r 身上，他只是碰巧是新来的。我们可以从 p 、 q 、 a 和 b 中选择任意一对向量作为同一空间的有效基。线性相关性问题涉及的是整个集合，而非某个特定向量。相反，如果我们的第三个基向量被选为任何其他不在 p 和 q 所构成的平面上的向量（例如，向量 c ），那么该基向量将是线性独立的，并且具有满秩。如果一组基向量是线性独立的，那么就不可能将任何一个基向量表示为其他基向量的线性组合。

So a set of linearly dependent vectors is certainly a poor choice for a basis. But there are other more stringent properties we might desire of a basis. To see this, let's return to coordinate space transformations. Assume, as before. that we have an object whose basis vectors are p , q , and r , and we know the coordinates of these vectors in world space. Let b =[bx,by,bz] be the coordinates of some arbitrary vector in body space, and u =[ux,uy,uz] be the coordinates of that same vector, in upright space. From our robot example, we already know the relationship between u and b :
因此，一组线性相关的向量作为基肯定不是一个好的选择。但是，我们可能希望基具有其他更严格的属性。为了说明这一点，让我们回到坐标空间变换。像以前一样假设，我们有一个物体，其基向量为 p 、 q 和 r ，并且我们知道这些向量在世界空间中的坐标。令 b =[bx,by,bz] 为身体空间中某个任意向量的坐标，令 u =[ux,uy,uz] 为同一向量在直立空间中的坐标。从我们的机器人示例中，我们已经知道 u 和 b 之间的关系：

ux=bxpx+byqx+bzrx, u =bx p +by q +bz r ,or equivalently,uy=bxpy+byqy+bzry,uz=bxpz+byqz+bzrz.

Make sure you understand the relationship between these equations and Equation (3.1) before moving on.
在继续之前，请确保您理解这些方程与方程 (3.1) 之间的关系。

Now here's the key problem: what if u is known and b is the vector we're trying to determine? To illustrate the profound difference between these two questions, let's write the two systems side-by-side, replacing the unknown vector with “?”:
现在关键问题来了：如果 u 已知，而 b 是我们要确定的向量，会怎么样？为了说明这两个问题之间的巨大差异，我们并排写出这两个系统，并将未知向量替换为“？”：

?x=bxpx+byqx+bzrx,ux=?xpx+?yqx+?zrx,?y=bxpy+byqy+bzry,uy=?xpy+?yqy+?zry,?z=bxpz+byqz+bzrz,uz=?xpz+?yqz+?zrz.

The system of equations on the left is not really much of a “system” at all, it's just a list; each equation is independent, and each unknown quantity can be immediately computed from a single equation. On the right, however, we have three interrelated equations, and none of the unknown quantities can be determined without all three equations. In fact, if the basis vectors are linearly dependent, then the system on the right may have zero solutions ( u is not in the span), or it might have an infinite number of solutions ( u is in the span and the coordinates are not uniquely determined). We hasten to add that the critical distinction is not between upright or body space; we are just using those spaces to have a specific example. The important fact is whether the known coordinates of the vector being transformed are expressed relative to the basis (the easy situation on the left), or if the coordinates of the vector and the basis vectors are all expressed in the same coordinate space (the hard situation on theright).
左边的方程组实际上根本算不上一个“系统”，它只是一个列表；每个方程都是独立的，每个未知量都可以直接从一个方程计算出来。然而，右边的方程组有三个相互关联的方程，没有这三个方程就无法确定任何未知量。事实上，如果基向量是线性相关的，那么右边的方程组可能没有解（ u 不在跨度内），也可能有无数个解（ u 在跨度内，并且坐标不唯一确定）。我们赶紧补充一点，关键的区别不在于直立空间还是身体空间；我们只是用这些空间来举一个具体的例子。重要的事实是，被变换向量的已知坐标是相对于基向量表示的（左边的简单情况），还是向量和基向量的坐标都在同一个坐标空间中表示（右边的困难情况）。

Linear algebra provides a number of general-purpose tools for solving systems of linear equations like this, but we don't need to delve into these topics, because the solution to this system is not our primary aim. For now, we're interested in understanding one special situation for which the solution is easy. (In Section 6.2, we show how to use the matrix inverse to solve the general case.)
线性代数提供了许多通用的工具来求解这类线性方程组，但我们无需深入研究这些主题，因为求解这类方程组并非我们的主要目标。目前，我们感兴趣的是理解一种特殊情况，这种情况下求解起来比较容易。（在 6.2 节中，我们将展示如何使用矩阵逆来求解这种一般情况。）

The dot product is the key. Remember from Section 2.11.2 that the dot product can be used to measure distance in a particular direction. As we observed in that same section, when using the standard basis p =[1,0,0] , q =[0,1,0] , and r =[0,0,1] , corresponding to the object axes being parallel with the world axes in our robot example, we can dot the vector with a basis vector to “sift out” the corresponding coordinate.
点积是关键。记得 2.11.2 节说过，点积可以用来测量特定方向上的距离。正如我们在同一节中观察到的，当使用标准基向量 p =[1,0,0] 、 q =[0,1,0] 和 r =[0,0,1] 时（这对应于机器人示例中物体轴与世界轴平行的情况），我们可以将向量与基向量点积，从而“筛选出”相应的坐标。

bx= u ⋅ p = u ⋅ [ 1 0 0 ] =uxby= u ⋅ q = u ⋅ [ 0 1 0 ] =uybz= u ⋅ r = u ⋅ [ 0 0 1 ] =uz

Algebraically, this is rather obvious. But does this “sifting” action work for any arbitrary basis? Sometimes, but not always. In fact, we can see that it doesn't work for the example we have been using. Figure 3.13 compares the correct coordinates ax and ay with the dot products a ⋅ p and a ⋅ q . (The illustration is completely correct only if p and q are unit vectors.)
从代数上来说，这相当明显。但这种“筛选”操作对任意基都有效吗？有时有效，但并非总是如此。事实上，我们可以看到，它对我们之前使用的示例并不适用。图 3.13 将正确的坐标 ax 和 ay 与点积 a ⋅ p 和 a ⋅ q 进行了比较。（只有当 p 和 q 为单位向量时，该图才完全正确。）

Figure 3.13  图 3.13 The dot product doesn't “sift out” the coordinate in this case.
在这种情况下，点积不会“筛选出”坐标。

Notice that, in each case, the result produced by the dot product is larger than the correct coordinate value. To understand what's wrong, we need to go back and correct a little lie that we told in Chapter 1. We said that a coordinate measures the displacement from the origin in a given direction; this displacement is exactly what the dot product is measuring. While that is the simplest way to explain coordinates, it works only under special circumstances. (Our lie isn't that harmful because these circumstances are very common!) Now that we understand basis vectors, we're ready for the more complete description.
请注意，在每种情况下，点积的结果都大于正确的坐标值。为了理解问题所在，我们需要回过头来纠正我们在第一章中说过的一个小谎。我们说坐标测量的是给定方向上相对于原点的位移；这个位移正是点积测量的。虽然这是解释坐标最简单的方法，但它只在特殊情况下有效。（我们的谎言并没有那么有害，因为这些情况非常常见！）现在我们理解了基向量，就可以进行更完整的描述了。

The numeric coordinates of a vector with respect to a given basis are the coefficients in the expansion of that vector as a linear combination of the basis vectors. For example, a =ax p +ay q .
向量相对于给定基的数值坐标是该向量展开式中系数，该展开式为基向量的线性组合。例如， a =ax p +ay q 。

The reason the dot product doesn't “sift out” the coordinates in Figure 3.13 is because we are ignoring the fact that y q will cause some displacement parallel to p . To visualize this, imagine that we increased ax while holding ay constant. As a moves to the right and slightly upwards, its projection onto q , which is measured by the dot product, increases.
图 3.13 中点积之所以没有“滤除”坐标，是因为我们忽略了 y q 会导致平行于 p 的位移。为了直观地理解这一点，假设我们增加 ax ，同时保持 ay 不变。当 a 向右略微向上移动时，它在 q 上的投影（由点积测量）会增加。

The problem is that the basis vectors are not perpendicular. A set of basis vectors that are mutually perpendicular is called an orthogonal basis.
问题在于基向量不垂直。一组相互垂直的基向量称为正交基。

When the basis vectors are orthogonal, the coordinates are uncoupled. Any given coordinate of a vector v can be determined solely from v and the corresponding basis vector. For example, we can compute vx knowing only p , provided that the other basis vectors are perpendicular to p .
当基向量正交时，坐标系是解耦的。向量 v 的任何给定坐标都可以仅通过 v 和相应的基向量确定。例如，只要其他基向量垂直于 p ，我们就可以仅知道 p 来计算 vx 。

Although we won't investigate it further in this book, the idea of orthonormal basis is a broadly powerful one with applications outside our immediate concerns. For example, it is the idea behind Fourier analysis.
虽然本书不会深入探讨，但正交基的概念非常强大，其应用范围远超我们当前关注的范畴。例如，它就是傅里叶分析背后的思想。

If it's good when basis vectors are orthogonal, then it's best when they all have unit length. Such a set of vectors are known as an orthonormal basis. Why is the unit length helpful? Remember the geometric definition of the dot product: a ⋅ p is equal to the signed length of a projected onto p , times the length of p . If the basis vector doesn't have unit length, but it is perpendicular to all the others, we can still determine the corresponding coordinate with the dot product; we just need to divide by the square of the length of the basis vector.
如果基向量正交是好的，那么最好它们都具有单位长度。这样的一组向量被称为正交基。为什么单位长度有用？记住点积的几何定义： a ⋅ p 等于 a 投影到 p 上的带符号长度乘以 p 的长度。如果基向量不是单位长度，但它与所有其他基向量垂直，我们仍然可以用点积确定相应的坐标；我们只需除以基向量长度的平方即可。

In an orthonormal basis, each coordinate of a vector v is the signed displacement v measured in the direction of the corresponding basis vector. This can be computed directly by taking the dot product of v with that basis vector.
在正交基中，向量 v 的每个坐标都是在相应基向量方向上测量的带符号位移 v 。这可以通过将 v 与该基向量进行点积直接计算得出。

Thus, in the special circumstance of an orthonormal basis, we have a simple way to determine the body space coordinates, knowing only the world coordinates of the body axes. Thus, assuming p , q , and r form an orthonormal basis,
因此，在正交基的特殊情况下，我们只需知道身体轴的世界坐标，就可以简单地确定身体空间坐标。因此，假设 p 、 q 和 r 构成一个正交基，

bx= u ⋅ p ,by= u ⋅ q ,bz= u ⋅ r .

Although our example uses body space and upright space for concreteness, these are general ideas that apply to any coordinate space transformation.
尽管我们的示例为了具体起见使用了身体空间和直立空间，但这些是适用于任何坐标空间变换的一般思想。

Orthonormal bases are the special circumstances under which our lie from Chapter 1 is harmless; fortunately they are extremely common. At the beginning of this section, we mentioned that most of the coordinate spaces we are “accustomed to” have certain properties. All of these “customary” coordinate spaces have an orthonormal basis, and in fact they meet an even further restriction: the coordinate space is not mirrored. That is, p × q = r , and the axes obey the prevailing handedness conventions (in this book, we use the left-hand conventions). A mirrored basis where p × q =− r can still be an orthonormal basis.
正交基是第一章中提到的特殊情况，在这种情况下不会造成任何损害；幸运的是，它们极其常见。在本节开头，我们提到大多数我们“习惯”的坐标空间都具有某些属性。所有这些“习惯”的坐标空间都具有正交基，事实上，它们还满足一个更进一步的限制：坐标空间不是镜像的。也就是说， p × q = r ，并且坐标轴遵循普遍的惯用手性约定（本书中，我们使用左手约定）。镜像基，其中 p × q =− r 仍然可以是正交基。

3.4Nested Coordinate Spaces
3.4 嵌套坐标空间

Each object in a 3D virtual universe has its own coordinate space—its own origin and its axes. Its origin could be located at its center of mass, for example. Its axes specify which directions it considers to be “up,” “right,” and “forward” relative to its origin. A 3D model created by an artist for a virtual world will have its origin and axes decided by the artist, and the points that make up the polygon mesh will be relative to the object space defined by this origin and axes. For example, the center of a sheep could be placed at (0,0,0) , the tip of its snout at (0,0,1.5) , the tip if its tail at (0,0,−1.2) , and the tip of its right ear at (0.5,0.2,1.2) . These are the locations of these parts in sheep space.
3D 虚拟宇宙中的每个对象都有自己的坐标空间 - 自己的原点和轴。例如，它的原点可以位于其质心。它的轴指定相对于原点的“上”、“右”和“前”的方向。艺术家为虚拟世界创建的 3D 模型的原点和轴由艺术家决定，构成多边形网格的点将相对于此原点和轴定义的对象空间。例如，绵羊的中心可以放在 (0,0,0) 处，鼻子尖端放在 (0,0,1.5) 处，尾巴尖端放在 (0,0,−1.2) 处，右耳尖放在 (0.5,0.2,1.2) 处。这些是这些部分在绵羊空间中的位置。

The position and orientation of an object at any point in time needs be specified in world coordinates so that we can compute the interactions between nearby objects. To be precise, we must specify the location and orientation of the object's axes in world coordinates. To specify the city of Cartesia's position (see Section 1.2.1) in world space, we could state that the origin is at longitude p o and latitude q o and that the positive x -axis points east and the positive y -axis points north. To locate the sheep in a virtual world, it is sufficient to specify the location of its origin and the orientation of its axes in world space. The world location of the tip of its snout, for example, can be worked out from the relative position of its snout to the world coordinates of its origin. But if the sheep is not actually being drawn, we can save effort by keeping track of only the location and orientation of its object space in world space. It becomes necessary to compute the world coordinates of its snout, tail, and right ear at only certain times—for example, when it moves into view of the camera.
为了计算邻近物体之间的相互作用，我们需要在世界坐标系中指定物体在任何时间点的位置和方向。准确地说，我们必须在世界坐标系中指定物体坐标轴的位置和方向。为了在世界空间中指定笛卡尔城的位置（参见 1.2.1 节），我们可以指定原点位于经度 p o 和纬度 q o ，正 x 轴指向东，正 y 轴指向北。要在虚拟世界中定位绵羊，只需指定其原点的位置及其坐标轴在世界空间中的方向即可。例如，可以根据其鼻子相对于原点的世界坐标的相对位置推导出其鼻子尖端的世界位置。但如果没有实际绘制绵羊，我们可以节省精力，只需跟踪其物体空间在世界空间中的位置和方向。仅在某些时候才需要计算其鼻子、尾巴和右耳的世界坐标 - 例如，当它进入摄像机视野时。

Since the object space moves around in world space, it is convenient to view the world space as a “parent” space, and the object space as a “child” space. It is also convenient to break objects into subobjects and to animate them independently. A model decomposed into a hierarchy like this is sometimes called an articulated model. For example, as the sheep walks, its head swings back and forth and its ears flap up and down. In the coordinate space of the sheep's head, the ears appear to be flapping up and down—the motion is in the y -axis only and so is relatively easy to understand and animate. In the sheep's coordinate space its head is swinging from side to side along the sheep's x -axis, which is again relatively easy to understand. Now, suppose that the sheep is moving along the world's z -axis. Each of the three actions—ears flapping, head swinging, and sheep moving forwards—involves a single axis and is easy to understand in isolation from the others. The motion of the tip of the sheep's right ear, however, traces a complicated path through the world coordinate space, truly a nightmare for a programmer to compute from scratch. By breaking the sheep into a hierarchically organized sequence of objects with nested coordinate spaces, however, the motion can be computed in separate components and combined relatively easily with linear algebra tools such as matrices and vectors, as we see in later chapters.
由于对象空间在世界空间中移动，因此将世界空间视为“父”空间，将对象空间视为“子”空间会很方便。将对象分解为子对象并分别设置动画也很方便。分解成这种层次结构的模型有时被称为铰接模型。例如，当绵羊行走时，它的头会前后摆动，耳朵也会上下拍动。在绵羊头部的坐标空间中，耳朵看起来是在上下拍动——运动仅在 y 轴上进行，因此相对容易理解和设置动画。在绵羊的坐标空间中，它的头沿着绵羊的 x 轴左右摆动，这也相对容易理解。现在，假设绵羊沿着世界坐标系的 z 轴移动。这三个动作——拍动耳朵、摆动头部和向前移动——都只涉及一个轴，因此很容易与其他动作分开理解。然而，绵羊右耳尖的运动在世界坐标空间中轨迹复杂，对于程序员来说，从零开始计算简直是一场噩梦。然而，通过将绵羊分解成具有嵌套坐标空间的层级结构的对象序列，运动可以分解成单独的分量进行计算，并相对容易地与矩阵和向量等线性代数工具结合起来，正如我们在后面的章节中看到的那样。

For example, let's say we need to know the world coordinates of the tip of the ear of the sheep. To compute these coordinates, we might first use what we know about the relationship of the sheep's ear relative to its head to compute the coordinates of that point in “head space.” Next, we use the position and orientation of the head relative to the body to compute the coordinates in “body space.” Finally, since we know the position and orientation of the sheep's body relative to the world's origin and axes, we can compute the coordinates in world space. The next few chapters go deeper into the details of how to do this.
例如，假设我们需要知道羊耳朵尖的世界坐标。为了计算这些坐标，我们首先可以利用已知的羊耳朵相对于头部的位置关系，计算出该点在“头部空间”中的坐标。接下来，我们利用头部相对于身体的位置和方向，计算出“身体空间”中的坐标。最后，由于我们知道羊身体相对于世界原点和坐标轴的位置和方向，我们就可以计算出它在世界空间中的坐标。接下来的几章将深入探讨如何做到这一点。

It's convenient to think of the sheep's coordinate space moving relative to world space, the sheep's head coordinate space moving relative to the sheep's space, and the sheep's ear space moving relative to the sheep's head space. Thus we view the head space as a child of the sheep space, and the ear space as a child of the head space. Object space can be divided into many different subspaces at many different levels, depending on the complexity of the object being animated. We can say that the child coordinate space is nested in the parent coordinate space. This parent-child relationship between coordinate spaces defines a hierarchy, or tree, of coordinate spaces. The world coordinate space is the root of this tree. The nested coordinate space tree can change dynamically during the lifetime of a virtual world; for example, the sheep's fleece can be sheared and taken away from the sheep, and thus the fleece coordinate space goes from being a child of the sheep body's coordinate space to being a child of the world space. The hierarchy of nested coordinate spaces is dynamic and can be arranged in a manner that is most convenient for the information that is importantto us.
可以方便地想象绵羊的坐标空间相对于世界空间移动，绵羊头部的坐标空间相对于绵羊自身空间移动，绵羊耳朵的空间相对于绵羊头部空间移动。因此，我们将头部空间视为绵羊空间的子空间，将耳朵空间视为头部空间的子空间。根据动画对象的复杂程度，对象空间可以划分为许多不同级别的子空间。我们可以说子坐标空间嵌套在父坐标空间中。坐标空间之间的这种父子关系定义了坐标空间的层次结构或树。世界坐标空间是这棵树的根。嵌套的坐标空间树可以在虚拟世界的生命周期内动态变化；例如，羊毛可以被剪掉并从绵羊身上取下，因此羊毛坐标空间从绵羊身体坐标空间的子空间变为世界坐标空间的子空间。嵌套坐标空间的层次结构是动态的，并且可以按照对我们重要的信息最方便的方式进行排列。

3.5In Defense of Upright Space
3.5 捍卫直立空间

Finally, please allow us a few paragraphs to try to persuade you that the concept of upright space is highly useful, even though the term may not be standard. Lots9 of people don't bother distinguishing between world space and upright space. They would just talk about rotating a vector from object space to “world space.” But consider the common situation in code when the same data type, say float3, is used to store both “points” and “vectors.” (See Section 2.4 if you don't remember why those terms were just put in quotes.) Let's say we have one float3 that represents the position of a vertex in object space, and we wish to know the position of that vertex in world space. The transformation from object to world space must involve translation by the object's position. Now compare this to a different float3 that describes a direction, such as a surface normal or the direction a gun is aiming.
